digest.component_or_area: Store write lock acquisition and retry mechanism
propositions: Write operations whose lock acquisition times out are permanently discarded with no retry or queue mechanism, making loss terminal and lossy rather than converting it to latency
The current acquire() implementation computes a single deadline from timeout*attempts but never retries on expiration, so attempts is a silent multiplier not a retry loop

Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() (with retries parameter defaulting to 0 for backward compatibility) converts timed-out acquisitions into latency by re-attempting passes with jittered exponential backoff and intermediate release windows
Five call sites opted into retries via _write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped [0,10]): three in event_append.py, one each in txn.py and push.py

Retry safety is assured because LockTimeout is raised by acquire() before the write body executes, making re-attempts impossible to double-append, and the retry loop lives strictly inside acquire() rather than above it
